issue.title: fix(hogql): print is null as a null check in join constraints
issue.body:
## Problem

- HogQL queries with `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL` in a JOIN ON clause match no rows from the joined table.
- It happens when ON has no `team_id` guard: inner joins, and LEFT JOINs onto warehouse tables, views, or subqueries.
- The printer emits `equals(x, NULL)` there, and ClickHouse evaluates that to NULL.

## Changes

- A literal NULL comparison in JOIN ON now prints `isNull(x)` or `isNotNull(x)`, as WHERE does since #115021.
- LEFT JOINs onto team-scoped tables already print this form in ON, because the guard path skips the join-constraint check.
- Column-to-column join keys keep the unwrapped `equals()`.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_equals_null` failed before the fix with `equals(b.distinct_id, NULL)` in ON.
- No snapshot prints a NULL comparison inside ON.

**Test rationale:** Catches a reintroduced join exemption. `test_equals_null` covered only expressions outside joins.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

issue.title: Feature request: cmd+k - see all persons that match a search when more than 5 match
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Searching for people by company name in Cmd+K, for example `acme`, leaves some existing people out of the results. The Persons section shows at most 5 matches, most recently created first, and nothing shows that more people match. Anyone older than the 5 newest matches can't be reached from the search.

When more people match a Cmd+K search than the Persons section shows, a way to see all of them from the search, for example a row that opens the Persons list with the same search filled in.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Searching a person's full email in Cmd+K finds them, but only when you already know the exact email.

issue.title: fix(mcp-store): negotiate the mcp protocol version when syncing tools

labels.name: repo-b94bc5f2
labels.description: Skip the check that blocks desktop and backend changes in one PR

issue.body:
Thanks to [tm2998](https://github.com/tm2998), who diagnosed this bug and proposed the fix in #126524, and to [Christiaan](https://github.com/christiaan-ph), whose #127525 is included here.

## Problem

- GitLab connections in the MCP store list zero tools. The sync offers protocol `2024-11-05`, and GitLab rejects it with HTTP 400 (#126521).
- Agent links to an MCP server page use the connection id, so the page fails to load.

Closes #126521

## Changes

- GitLab connections list their tools again. The sync offers `2025-06-18`, falls back when a server rejects the offer, and sends `MCP-Protocol-Version`.
- New events: `mcp_store tools synced`, with `protocol_version`, and `mcp_store tools sync failed`.
- `mcp-connections-list` returns `gateway_server_id`, from #127525.
- The agent sharing copy on the server page now matches how grants resolve.
- Firetiger is hidden from the catalog, because its host does not resolve.
- Existing connections with zero tools stay empty until they sync again. A resync follows the deploy.
- The rest is mechanical.


## How did you test this code?

- Live GitLab: `2024-11-05` returns 400. The branch negotiates `2025-06-18` and lists 39 tools.
- Not checked: the GitLab OAuth path, which runs the same sync code. The copy was not rendered.

**Test rationale:** new cases cover the fallback, the stop on 401, and both sync events.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

- None.

issue.title: Bug report: PostHog AI - tag-like text disappears from the user's chat messages
issue.body:
In PostHog AI chat, text in the user's own message that looks like an HTML tag is missing from the message shown in the chat history. For example, sending `Repeat this back exactly: keep <example> intact` displays as `Repeat this back exactly: keep  intact`. PostHog AI still receives the full text. Tags in PostHog AI's replies are hidden the same way unless the reply puts them in code formatting, so a reply can show a tag that the user's own message above it doesn't. This happens on both the LangGraph and sandbox chat runtimes.

Expected: the user's message displays exactly what was typed.

## How to reproduce

1. Open PostHog AI and send `Repeat this back exactly: keep <example> intact`
2. Look at your message in the chat history: `<example>` is missing

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/80920

Messages are displayed through [`MarkdownMessage`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/28308e3b8224de83a0abf6c1e9f3a18aa6491362/products/posthog_ai/frontend/messages/MarkdownMessage.tsx#L27).

Related: #101455 fixed a similar case for agent object tags in PostHog AI replies. The same symptom in support tickets: #130066.

issue.body:

issue.title: fix(aio): retry byok 429s from first-party providers
issue.body:
## Problem

- BYOK teams on OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini lose every LLM judge evaluation on a key after a burst of 429s.
- Recovery takes a key re-validation plus a re-enable on each evaluation.
- #123445 added retries for custom endpoints only.

## Changes

- A 429 now retries after the provider's delay. When retries run out, the run is skipped and nothing is disabled.
- The OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini adapters raise `RetryableRateLimitError`. Azure inherits it.
- The judge and tagger turn off SDK retries. Stacked retries could overrun the 6-minute activity timeout.
- A Gemini 429 with a `RetryInfo` delay counts as a rate limit, not exhausted quota.
- Taggers stop marking the key as errored on a 429.
- Mechanical: the OpenAI-compatible adapter drops its own 429 override.

## How did you test this code?

- New 429 tests for each adapter fail on master.
- Not run: database-backed classes in `test_run_evaluation.py` (no local Postgres).

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-prs`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Christiaan opened the PR. Bernat took it over after a review found the two gaps above.
- **Decisions:** the fix sits in the adapters, not the judge, so each provider's delay survives.
- **Decisions:** `Client(max_retries=0)` applies only to the Temporal callers. The playground and task titles keep SDK retries.
- **Decisions:** Gemini reads the delay from the `google.rpc.RetryInfo` body detail, because Google sends no header.
- **Read closely:** `OpenAIAdapter._mapped_error`, the base for Azure, OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks, MiniMax and the OpenAI-compatible adapter.

issue.title: Feature request: metrics - include the time range in a shareable PromQL query
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

A Metrics alpha user wants to share a PromQL query with colleagues by pasting it into a Confluence page or a Slack message. The time range of a Metrics chart is set in the chart controls, not in the query text, so the pasted query does not carry the window it was written for and the reader has to set the range by hand. ## Describe the solution you'd like

A way to include the time range in the PromQL query, so that sharing the query text on its own is enough for a colleague to open the same chart over the same window.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Copying the Metrics page URL shares the query and the date range, but not the chart interval.

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/79941

issue.title: Feature request: self-driving - remember the scouts roster filter between visits
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

On the scouts roster (`/inbox/scouts`), a user who sets the filter to "Turned on" to see only their enabled scouts gets "All scouts" again the next time they open the page. The filter is kept in the URL, so it survives a refresh or a shared link. A fresh load of `/inbox/scouts`, such as a new tab or a later session, starts unfiltered, so the user has to pick "Turned on" again on every visit.

## Describe the solution you'd like

The scouts roster opens with the filter the user last chose, so a user who only works with enabled scouts doesn't have to set it on every visit.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Bookmarking the roster with the filter in the URL, `/inbox/scouts?scoutEnabled=enabled`, opens it filtered. This only helps when the user opens the roster from that bookmark.

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/79568 (EU Cloud)

- #87575 added the roster filters to the URL so a filtered view survives a refresh and can be shared. Remembering the choice between visits was not part of that change.
- The inbox report list keeps its scope and sort between visits (saved in the browser), so the two lists in the inbox behave differently.
- The roster's tag and owner filters work the same way as the "Turned on" filter. The roster's sort is not in the URL, so it resets on a refresh as well.

issue.title: Feature request: mcp analytics - name custom harnesses instead of showing them as Other
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

The harness charts in MCP Analytics only name clients on a built-in list that PostHog recognizes. Calls from a team's own in-house harness land under **Other harnesses** on the "Share of calls by harness" card and under **Unrecognized harnesses** in the "All harnesses" table, mixed in with every other client PostHog doesn't recognize. There is no setting in the UI to name the harness, so on these charts its traffic can't be told apart from other unrecognized clients.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A way for a team to register its own harnesses in MCP Analytics, set up in the UI: match calls by the client name or User-Agent pattern the harness reports, show them under a display name the team picks, and optionally add a logo or icon. The custom name should show up everywhere harnesses appear, including the share card, the "All harnesses" table, and the activity and session views.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

A custom SQL insight that splits out the harness's calls, or a PostHog code change to add each in-house harness to the built-in list. The user wants to avoid needing either.

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/79658

issue.title: fix(logs): filter renamed custom column cells on the attribute they read
issue.body:
## Problem

- Logs users who rename a custom column get include and exclude filters from its cells that do nothing.
- Exclude keeps every row, and include returns no logs. Nothing warns the user that the filter is wrong.
- The cell used the column label as the filter key, so a renamed column filtered on an attribute that does not exist.
- #113920 fixed the filter type for these cells and left renamed columns out of scope.
- Reported in a [support ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a162cc-d63c-0000-01c2-67f9fce28a91), where excluding four services from a column named "Service" removed none of them.

## Changes

- Include and exclude on a renamed custom column cell now filter on the attribute the column reads, so the expected rows go or stay.
- `customColumnFilterTarget` replaces `customColumnFilterType` and reads the key from the column expression, not the label:

| Column expression | Filter key and type |
| --- | --- |
| `attributes.<key>` | `<key>`, log attribute |
| `resource_attributes.<key>` | `<key>`, resource attribute |
| "Add as column" lookup | `<key>`, per row as before |
| `service_name` | `service_name`, log column |
| Other HogQL | The label, log attribute, as before |

- The cell popover's add and remove column button still matches on the label, because columns are found by name. `AttributeCell` takes a separate `filterKey` for this reason.
- Columns that keep their default name produce the same filters as before.
- Nothing looks different. Only the filter that a cell action adds changes.

- Three cases added to the parameterized `customColumnFilterTarget` test in `columns.test.ts`: a renamed `resource_attributes.<key>` column, a renamed "Add as column" column with an escaped key, and a renamed `service_name` column.
- With the previous logic swapped back in, those three fail and the six existing cases pass.
- A Playwright run on a local dev stack used seeded logs from four services and a custom column on `resource_attributes.service.name` named "Service":

| Cell action on `checkout-svc` | Base commit | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exclude as filter | `Service` log attribute filter, all 28 logs remain | `service.name` resource attribute filter, 20 logs, none from `checkout-svc` |
| Add as filter | `Service` log attribute filter, no results | `service.name` resource attribute filter, 8 logs, all from `checkout-svc` |

1. In Logs, open "Configure columns" and add `service.name` from Resource attributes.
2. Edit that column, set its name to "Service", and save.
3. Hover a value in the Service column and click "Exclude as filter".
4. Expected: the filter chip names `service.name` and rows from that service disappear. On master the chip names `Service` and every row stays.

**Test rationale:** The regression is a renamed custom column cell that filters on its label. The closest existing test is the `customColumnFilterType` table, and every case there names the column after its key, so it could not catch this. A pure function test is the lowest level that sees a wrong key.

issue.title: fix(desktop): exclude sleep time from the generated in duration
issue.body:
## Problem

- PostHog Desktop users see a very large "Generated in" time (for example 1341m) when the computer sleeps or shuts down during a turn.
- The footer duration is wall-clock time from prompt to turn completion. No code reacts to sleep, so asleep time counts as generation time.
- Permission waits already go into `pausedDurationMs` through `resolvePermission`. Sleep and app restarts do not.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a103ce-e653-7698-8d73-1da522958fb3 -->
## Origin

- Conversations: [ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a10387-5f97-0000-a927-6deac0602b57)
- First signal: 2026-10-03
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a103ce-e653-7698-8d73-1da522958fb3)
- Likely cause: [`abd278d`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/abd278d673e0b539556e105875e6eaa7a0e5ceee)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P3 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a103ce-e653-7698-8d73-1da522958fb3 -->

## Changes

- **Sleep detection:** the existing 30 s local silence check records when it last ran. When it fires more than 90 s late, the computer was asleep. The check adds that time to `pausedDurationMs` of each pending local turn. The live "Generating" timer and the final footer both subtract it.
  - Cloud turns are not changed, because a cloud agent keeps working while the laptop sleeps.
  - Turns with a pending permission are not changed, because the permission wait already counts that time.
  - The 90 s margin is above Chromium's one-minute timer throttling for hidden windows.
- **Fallback:** the conversation builder records the longest gap between two events of a turn. The footer hides the duration when a gap longer than 30 min is not explained by paused time. This covers a shutdown or app restart mid-turn, where no paused time survives.
- **Mechanical:** `ConversationView` and `ChatThreadFooter` now share one `lastGenerationDurationMs` helper.

> [!NOTE]
> A local tool call that is silent for more than 30 min also hides the duration. Hiding the label is better than showing a wrong value.

## How did you test this code?

- Added `it.each` cases to `sessionEventDiagnostics.test.ts`: a 2 h clock jump adds 2 h of paused time, and a 60 s throttled timer adds none.
- Added `it.each` cases to `buildConversationItems.test.ts`: a short turn, a permission wait explained by paused time, and an overnight gap that hides the duration.

- Not done: a manual sleep and wake of the Electron app. The sandbox cannot suspend the system.

**Test rationale:** the core cases fail if the sleep detection is removed or if timer throttling counts as sleep. The builder cases fail if the gap fallback is removed or hides normal turns. The closest existing tests (silence warning, `lastTurnInfo` shape) do not check durations across gaps.

issue.title: fix(logs): filter renamed custom column cells on the attribute they read
issue.body:
## Problem

- Logs users who rename a custom column get include and exclude filters from its cells that do nothing.
- Exclude keeps every row, and include returns no logs. Nothing warns the user that the filter is wrong.
- The cell used the column label as the filter key, so a renamed column filtered on an attribute that does not exist.
- #113920 fixed the filter type for these cells and left renamed columns out of scope.
- Reported in a [support ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a162cc-d63c-0000-01c2-67f9fce28a91), where excluding four services from a column named "Service" removed none of them.

## Changes

- Include and exclude on a renamed custom column cell now filter on the attribute the column reads, so the expected rows go or stay.
- `customColumnFilterTarget` replaces `customColumnFilterType` and reads the key from the column expression, not the label:

| Column expression | Filter key and type |
| --- | --- |
| `attributes.<key>` | `<key>`, log attribute |
| `resource_attributes.<key>` | `<key>`, resource attribute |
| "Add as column" lookup | `<key>`, per row as before |
| `service_name` | `service_name`, log column |
| Other HogQL | The label, log attribute, as before |

- The cell popover's add and remove column button still matches on the label, because columns are found by name. `AttributeCell` takes a separate `filterKey` for this reason.
- Columns that keep their default name produce the same filters as before.
- Nothing looks different. Only the filter that a cell action adds changes.

## How did you test this code?

- Three cases added to the parameterized `customColumnFilterTarget` test in `columns.test.ts`: a renamed `resource_attributes.<key>` column, a renamed "Add as column" column with an escaped key, and a renamed `service_name` column.
- With the previous logic swapped back in, those three fail and the six existing cases pass.
- A Playwright run on a local dev stack used seeded logs from four services and a custom column on `resource_attributes.service.name` named "Service":

| Cell action on `checkout-svc` | Base commit | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exclude as filter | `Service` log attribute filter, all 28 logs remain | `service.name` resource attribute filter, 20 logs, none from `checkout-svc` |
| Add as filter | `Service` log attribute filter, no results | `service.name` resource attribute filter, 8 logs, all from `checkout-svc` |

The assignee ran these steps by hand on a local dev stack, and all passed:

1. In Logs, open "Configure columns" and add `service.name` from Resource attributes.
2. Edit that column, set its name to "Service", and save.
3. Hover a value in the Service column and click "Exclude as filter".
4. Expected: the filter chip names `service.name` and rows from that service disappear. On master the chip names `Service` and every row stays.

**Test rationale:** The regression is a renamed custom column cell that filters on its label. The closest existing test is the `customColumnFilterType` table, and every case there names the column after its key, so it could not catch this. A pure function test is the lowest level that sees a wrong key.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- The work started from a support investigation. The filter in the ticket's URL keyed on the column label, which matched the gap #113920 left.

issue.title: Feature request: logs - include the log lines that triggered an alert in notifications
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

When a log alert fires, the notification it sends to Slack, Microsoft Teams, a webhook, or PagerDuty says how many logs matched and links to them, but doesn't include the log lines themselves. A user who acts on alerts straight from Teams, and raises tickets from the webhook for audit tracking, has to open PostHog for each alert to see which errors fired. An alert also notifies only when it starts firing and when it resolves, not when new matching logs arrive while it keeps firing ([docs](https://posthog.com/docs/logs/alerts#notification-cooldown)).

## Describe the solution you'd like

Include the log lines that matched the alert in its notifications, for every destination including webhooks: every matching line from the check window, with each line's timestamp and message. Let the alert's message template loop over those lines and read any log attribute, not only the message. For comparison, the user's current tool (Elasticsearch query alerts) lets an action template loop over the matching hits and print each one's timestamp and message.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- The "View logs" button in each notification opens Logs with the alert's filters over the window that check evaluated. It works, but needs a click through to PostHog for every alert.
- Editing a destination's message doesn't help, because the alert event it reads carries counts, filters, and links, but no log lines.

## Additional context

issue.body:
## Problem

- Readers of [Product analytics best practices](https://posthog.com/docs/product-analytics/best-practices#9-filter-out-internal-users) cannot act on section 9. It lists ways to exclude internal traffic, but it does not say where to set any of them up.
- The section does not cover the usual case on a personal or marketing site: your own anonymous visits.
- It recommends a custom `is_employee` property. posthog-js has `setInternalOrTestUser()` for this, and new projects filter out an **Internal / Test users** cohort by default.
- Origin: a [support ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a12b8e-113b-0000-40de-927cd31cd2cb) where a reader could not follow the section.

## Changes

- Section 9 starts with two steps: add a filter in **Filter out internal and test users**, then turn it on in each insight and in Web Analytics.
- Each kind of internal traffic names the property and the operator to use, with the labels the app shows. The kinds are team logins, local and staging sites, office IP addresses, and your own browser.
- A new "Exclude your own browser" part compares `setInternalOrTestUser()` with `opt_out_capturing()`.
- That part says both methods affect only the browser that calls them, and that the developer console only works with the HTML snippet.
- The email filter is now one example of a team property, because not every team shares an email domain.
- Terms such as person property, event property, and cohort link to their docs.
- Related: PostHog/posthog#115497 adds a note about anonymous events to [internal and test users](https://posthog.com/docs/data/test-accounts).

<details>
<summary>Where each claim comes from</summary>

- New projects get the cohort and a **user not in** filter: [`team.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/b99095c78f38ec562cb70a02789b08468760253e/posthog/models/team/team.py#L98-L109). Older projects get the cohort only from an unscheduled [backfill job](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/b99095c78f38ec562cb70a02789b08468760253e/posthog/dags/backfill_internal_test_users_cohort.py), which does not add the filter. The text tells readers to add both if they are missing.
- `setInternalOrTestUser()` sets `$internal_or_test_user`: [`posthog-core.ts#L4769`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/blob/9b7ef8478b7380dfa41c22cbeae2552caf88bdeb/packages/browser/src/posthog-core.ts#L4769).
- The opt-out state is stored per browser: [`consent.ts#L64`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/blob/9b7ef8478b7380dfa41c22cbeae2552caf88bdeb/packages/browser/src/consent.ts#L64).
- Only the snippet sets `window.posthog`, and the npm build does not: [`posthog-core.ts#L5422-L5427`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/blob/9b7ef8478b7380dfa41c22cbeae2552caf88bdeb/packages/browser/src/posthog-core.ts#L5422-L5427).
- `$host` includes the port: [`event-utils.ts#L248`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/blob/9b7ef8478b7380dfa41c22cbeae2552caf88bdeb/packages/browser-common/src/utils/event-utils.ts#L248).
- UI labels: [settings title](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/b99095c78f38ec562cb70a02789b08468760253e/frontend/src/scenes/settings/SettingsMap.tsx#L333-L334), [Web Analytics switch](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/b99095c78f38ec562cb70a02789b08468760253e/frontend/src/scenes/web-analytics/WebAnalyticsHeaderButtons.tsx#L75-L77), [operators](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/b99095c78f38ec562cb70a02789b08468760253e/frontend/src/lib/utils/operators.ts#L3-L11).

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [docs](https://posthog.com/handbook/wizard-and-docs/docs-style-guide) and/or [content](https://posthog.com/handbook/content/posthog-style-guide) style guides.
- [x] Words are spelled using American English
- [x] Use relative URLs for internal links
- [ ] I've checked the pages added or changed in the Vercel preview build
- [x] If I moved a page, I added a redirect in `vercel.json` (no page moved)

## How this was checked

- The page loads on a local dev server (`GATSBY_MINIMAL=true`), in light and dark mode. Section 9, the new subsection, and the table of contents render. This check ran before the last two commits, which only reword one bullet and remove one subsection.
- Each link target and heading anchor in the section exists in the source. The app link resolves through the `internal-user-filtering` setting alias.
- The console shows a 404 for `framework.js` and two SVG `width` warnings. `/docs/data/events` shows the same three on the same server, so this change does not cause them.
- `pnpm format` does not cover `.mdx` files. markdownlint ran in the pre-commit hook.
- Not checked yet: the Vercel preview build.

- Written by Claude Code (`claude-opus-5-5`), directed by a person who reviews the draft.
- Skills: `writing-user-facing-copy`, `writing-pr-descriptions`.
- Every behavior claim was checked against source in PostHog/posthog and PostHog/posthog-js. The links are in the collapsed section above.

issue.title: Bug report: desktop - setup script doesn't run until the Setup tab is clicked
issue.body:
In PostHog Desktop, an environment's setup script does not start when a new worktree task is created. The task shows a `Setup: <environment name>` tab with a loading spinner, but the script only begins running once that tab is clicked. The environment settings say the script "Runs in the worktree root right after it's created, before the agent starts." The agent also starts without waiting for the setup script to finish.

## How to reproduce

1. In PostHog Desktop, go to Settings > Environment and create an environment named `default` for a local repository, with the setup script `date > setup-ran.txt`.
2. Create a new local task in a worktree, pick the `default` environment in the worktree picker, and approve the setup script prompt.
3. Stay on the task's chat. The "Setup: default" tab shows a spinner, `setup-ran.txt` does not appear in the worktree, and the agent starts working.
4. Click the "Setup: default" tab. The script starts running and `setup-ran.txt` appears.

## Additional context

From support ticket 69215

Reported on `desktop-v0.61.22` (macOS). The setup dispatch code is unchanged on master as of `desktop-v0.61.671`. It starts at `dispatchEnvironmentSetup` in [taskCreationSaga.ts](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/desktop/packages/core/src/task-detail/taskCreationSaga.ts#L377-L389).
